`benmore feedback <app> [--status open|in_progress|resolved|wont_fix] [--env dev|prod]` lists the feedback visitors sent through the widget (MCP list_visitor_feedback), newest first; `--status` keeps one status. Actions: `show <id>`, `resolve <id>...`, `reopen <id>...`, `status <id> <state>`, `comment <id> <text>` and `delete <id>`. Editor access. Which instance a list or an id action reaches: api(at:"environments") context.

`benmore feedback-widget <app> [on|off] [--env dev|prod]` shows or sets `features.feedback` (see feedback_widget) in the selected instance's app.yaml. With no argument it prints the current state, read the way the app reads it: `feedback: yes`, `on` or `1` is on. `on` or `off` rewrites the `feedback:` line under `features:` whatever value it holds, or adds one under an existing `features:` block, as an ordinary source edit (validated, committed and reloaded like a push); an app.yaml without a `features:` block, or one that sets the switch inside a one-line `features: {...}` mapping, exits 1 and prints the lines to write. On an app with a dev instance the default target is dev and `benmore promote` carries the setting to prod; `--env prod` edits prod's app.yaml directly.
